content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem's causal chain, starting with the symptom that account pages failed for shoppers and citing the error rate spike from baseline to peak, then tracing into why the account page requests were failing.

Now I'm tracing the root cause: requests threw a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code between 16:42 and 16:48. Then I'm reasoning through why—the monthly-spend-feature flag flipped on just before that window and evaluations started returning on for most users, while an unrelated feature flag that also switched on is ruled out since it came after the onset time, and the deploy history shows no production changes correlated with the incident, with the revert of the spend flag alone restoring service while the unrelated flag stayed on.

That function only divides by the count of this-month purchases when the monthly-summary flag is true, which is empty for shoppers with past purchases but nothing this month — that's F1, confirmed by the matching line in G5309. Since this rests on an unrun reading rather than an S or D row, cause_rests_on_an_unrun_reading is true and reaches_a_cause is true.

So the chain should really be: the flag turning on is the trigger that enables the monthly-summary code path, and then that path divides by zero because the this-month purchase count is empty for shoppers without purchases this month.

I should frame this carefully as Code-Fix's reading of the unrun source rather than a verified fact. Root cause: the monthly spend summary path computes average spend per item by dividing the month's total by the number of this month's purchases without handling an empty list, so shoppers who've bought before but not this month hit a zero divisor, raising ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47, per F1.1.

For plain language I want to avoid number words entirely — so instead of "divides by zero," I'll phrase it as the calculation likely breaking when a shopper has no purchases yet this month, because it averages over an empty list. The faulty calculation remains in the code and still poses a risk until fixed.

For contributing factors, I'm noting that no test existed exercising the monthly-summary path for shoppers with past-but-not-current purchases before the flag went live — existing coverage only handled the lifetime case. Had that test existed, the fault likely would've been caught pre-production; merging the proposed fix with its tests only partially addresses this, so I should also flag the need for a pre-flip check on flag-gated code paths going forward.

Second factor: the rollout data shows the flag flipping from entirely off to entirely on within about a minute, with no staged rollout or gradual rollout gate evident. A progressive rollout with error-rate monitoring and auto-revert would have limited the blast radius, so I'll propose that as a process improvement.

For CF-3, nobody being paged doesn't seem like it would have shortened detection since Argus caught it quickly via the rule anyway — I'll skip that as a contributing factor.

For action items, I'm pulling together: requiring the account page test suite to pass with the flag on before production rollout (addresses CF-1), staging flag rollouts while watching error rates (addresses CF-2), and potentially an automatic revert mechanism when error rates spike after a toggle.

I'm deciding not to propose confirming the cause or re-running tests, since that's already covered by the review item, and the record already confirms the flag mitigation worked.

For lessons learned, I'm noting that Argus reverted the flag after the alert was raised and confirmed the fix.

Code-Fix drafted a fix with tests in PR #364, and the Investigator identified the leading candidate linking errors to the flag, all after the alert raised—consistent with the record. For what went wrong, I'm weighing whether to flag that nobody was paged and no on-call incident was linked, since it's a notable fact even if not clearly a failure, along with the issue that the flag was switched on by an admin without proper staffing oversight.

For the lucky break, I'm noting that a second, unrelated flag was toggled by an admin during the incident, which could have muddied attribution but didn't since reverting the original flag alone resolved things—so the second change never needed untangling.

I'm setting aside pre-existing baseline errors (like the earlier ClientDisconnected entries) as irrelevant, and I'm laying out my assumptions: the document's own reasoning rests on reading the fix rather than running it, the ZeroDivisionError lines are what's driving the failed account page requests despite being sampled, and the running revision stayed constant since no deploy occurred. Now I'm starting to build the causal chain, citing the key log sources and noting the peak error point at 16:45.

I'm ruling out alternative causes step by step: the unrelated feature flag came online after onset and recovery only happened when the monthly-spend feature was reverted, so that's eliminated. As for a deploy, none occurred the day before onset and all replicas stayed on one revision, so I'm checking whether the running revision itself could be ruled out — the service was healthy with this exact code in place based on metrics read between then and the onset, which supports ruling it out as the cause.

The requests that failed went through a code path gated by the monthly-spend-feature flag — it evaluated off before the admin enabled it, turned mostly on within a minute, then stayed on for every subsequent evaluation, and disabling it stopped the errors, confirming the link. For step four I'm citing the code fix reading and its source reference.

action_items.item: Add a pre-release check that runs the account page tests with monthly-spend-feature on, including a shopper with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out monthly-spend-feature, and other flags that change account pages, to a small share of shoppers first, and widen the rollout only while the account page error rate stays at its baseline.
Turn a newly switched-on flag back off automatically when the service's error rate rises soon after the change.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that returned server errors rose from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average while the service was broken, and peaked at {series_at_worst}. The service's own warning put the account page error rate as high as {Gbac1.5}, at {Gbac1.7}.
The account page requests failed because they raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors were logged from {G5309.3} and were not seen before the onset.

ruled_out.what: The flag change to an-unrelated-feature, switched on at {P2.1}. It came after the onset at {began}, and the service recovered when only monthly-spend-feature was reverted.

A deploy. No deploy came back from the day before the onset. As of {T10.1}, every replica ran one revision, and that revision was in place while account pages rendered normally and errors sat at their baseline before the onset.

causal_chain.step: The failing code runs only when monthly-spend-feature is on, and admin switched that flag on at {P1.1}. Before the onset the flag was off for every logged evaluation (G7e5d). In the minute of {G971b.6} most evaluations came back on (G971b), and every logged evaluation over {Gce95.4} came back on (Gce95). Once the flag was set back to off, the service was no longer at the incident's level from {T20.2}, and the action was judged confirmed.

When use_monthly_summary is true, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}, the line the logged error points to. This comes from Code-Fix's reading of the source.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary exposed a calculation that averages a shopper's spending over this month's purchases, and that calculation likely breaks when a shopper has bought before but not yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check was seen that ran the monthly summary path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month before monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Code-Fix's reading points only to an existing test for the lifetime-average case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The failing division would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production, and the incident would not have happened.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off for every logged evaluation to on for every logged evaluation within about a minute. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, with a check on the error rate, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit failing account pages before the error rise showed, and the flag could have been turned back off before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: admin switched on a second flag, an-unrelated-feature, at {P2.1}, while the incident was under way. Reverting monthly-spend-feature alone brought the service back. Had the second change also caused failures, the revert would not have been enough and the cause would have been harder to pick out.
went_well: The Investigator tied the errors to the monthly-spend-feature change, which became leading candidate C1, {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and the change can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix and two new tests, PR #364, {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: No person was paged when the alert fired: no on-call incident was linked to it.

input.root_cause: When monthly-spend-feature is on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the shopper's total for the month by the number of purchases made this month. Nothing in the files Code-Fix read handles the case where that list is empty, so for a shopper who has bought before but not this month the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and the page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The calculation that fails for shoppers with no purchases this month was still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make their account pages fail again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
